text:
For a diagnostic intended to isolate history substitutions, exclude the entire fixed candidate set—positive target and all sampled negatives—from replacement donors before sampling. Otherwise substitutions can place a scored candidate directly in the history, mixing contextual sensitivity with candidate exposure. Apply the same eligibility rule across interventions; report rejection rates, empty pools and effective donor counts. Keep candidates unchanged rather than deleting overlapping candidates after substitution. This is a design recommendation inferred from the diagnostic’s purpose, not a universal published rule; allowing overlap defines a different intervention. Interpret results as frozen-model sensitivity under the sampled protocol: sampled ranking metrics need not preserve full-catalog conclusions ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Compute paired intervention-minus-baseline differences for each substitution, average within user, then bootstrap users with the same resampled indices across every contrast. Repeated substitutions are not independent users ([SciPy paired bootstrap](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). With realized donors and candidates held fixed, intervals describe user variability conditional on those realizations; they do not separately establish robustness to new donor or candidate draws. To assess those sources, repeat donor sampling and, in a separate diagnostic sensitivity analysis, candidate sampling, preserving baseline/intervention pairing and the actual sampling hierarchy. Keep the pinned benchmark unchanged. Report donor Monte Carlo error separately; avoid mechanically adding nested resampling that double-counts variability already present in user-level estimates.

Predefine the family of reported contrasts. Use simultaneous bootstrap intervals or Bonferroni-adjusted intervals for familywise coverage; Holm-adjusted p-values address multiple tests but do not make ordinary 95% intervals simultaneous ([R documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/p.adjust.html)). All inference remains conditional on the single trained model and does not establish causal effects on user behavior.
